observation.visible_scene: A fixed-camera view of a sunset sky over a silhouetted foreground: a peaked-roof house on the right-center, a lattice/scaffold frame and a curved streetlight pole on the left, and a small steady orange lamp-glow on the building. Dark cumulus clouds are backlit by a bright yellow-orange sun gap near the horizon, with pinkish-grey sky above.
visible_changes: The cloud field continuously deforms and shifts across the frame while the camera and all foreground silhouettes stay in identical positions (no pan, tilt, or zoom).

The bright sunlit opening changes shape and position: in early frames it is a horizontal yellow band low on the right; by later frames it becomes a more vertical, narrower bright slot near the center-right, and the orange patch on the left widens.
The upper sky loses its orange tint and turns paler pink-grey, and the overall glow appears slightly dimmer toward the last frame, consistent with the sun sinking behind cloud.
Individual cloud lobes (e.g. the small blue-tinged bump on the right edge of the central mass) move relative to the static house roofline, confirming real cloud motion rather than camera motion.
The small orange lamp point on the building silhouette remains constant in position and brightness throughout, distinguishing it as an artificial light rather than reflected sunlight.
outside_clip_unknowns: The physical cause of the cloud drift (wind) is not visible.
Whether the dimming continues to full night, or the bright gap reopens, lies outside the cropped segment.
Any activity on or inside the silhouetted building is unseen.
uncertain_details: A single net translation direction for the clouds cannot be confidently assigned; different cloud masses appear to shift relative to one another (morphing plus slow drift) rather than translating uniformly.
Whether the slight overall darkening is true sunset progression or an exposure/tone change in the source clip is not determinable from the frames.
